text:
Zach Benson is doing almost everything a top-line winger does except score. At 21 he's playing 20:11 a night, the Sabres control 62% of the shot attempts at five-on-five when he's out there, and he's on the ice for 71% of their power-play chances. The Athletic just ran a piece calling him a star who has arrived. The goal column hasn't caught up: two goals on 7.95 expected goals (the quality of his chances), a 4% shooting rate against a league norm near 13%.

That gap is the story, and it's the kind that usually closes. He keeps getting to good ice; last season's All Three Zones tracking by Corey Sznajder had him taking 1.7 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net, the most dangerous looks in hockey. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play at the 98th percentile among forwards in 2025-26, so the territory he wins isn't new. He's pointless in his last four on 3.2 expected points, with the chances still there. If you're looking for one Sabre whose numbers understate how he's playing, it's this one.
